name: us-federal-tax
description: Dependency-free US federal tax engine for tax years 2024, 2025 and 2026: income tax brackets, Publication 15-T payroll withholding and paycheck math, self-employment tax, FICA, capital gains, NIIT, the child tax credit and EITC, the Section 199A QBI deduction, the SALT cap, the SECTION 86 taxation of Social Security benefits and quarterly estimated payments. Every figure cited to the IRS release it came from, including the OBBBA changes that apply retroactively to 2025. SECTION 86: the four thresholds that decide how much of a Social Security benefit is taxable - $25,000 and $32,000 set in 1983, $34,000 and $44,000 set in 1993 - have NEVER been indexed, and are the only figures in this package that are the same object in every tax year; a married filer filing separately who lived with their spouse at any time in the year has a base amount of ZERO, so 85% of the benefit is taxable from the first dollar and one fact about cohabitation is the difference between $17,000 and $0 of taxable benefit; tax-exempt municipal interest is added back in full, so $10,000 of it pulls $8,500 of benefit into taxable income exactly as taxable interest would; and because the provision INCLUDES benefit in income rather than taxing it at a rate, a dollar of other income inside the phase-in band drags up to 85 cents of untaxed benefit in behind it - the TAX TORPEDO, worth a 40.70% marginal rate in the 22% bracket. From 2025 to 2028 that composes with the OBBBA senior deduction, which phases out at 6% of MAGI excess PER ELIGIBLE PERSON while Section 86 is what moves MAGI, so a couple both 65 with a $90,000 benefit and $80,000 of other income face 45.58% on the next dollar - above the 37% top rate, in the 22% bracket, and 4.88 points HIGHER than the same couple faced in 2024, the year before they were given the deduction that cut their bill by $3,897.96. Their marginal rate reverses direction four times between $75,000 and $175,000 of other income without ever leaving the 22% and 24% brackets.
